the World Edit //pos1, //pos2 and //set commands are used.

the Carpet mod and thus the '/carpet fillUpdates false' rule available.

litematica.config.generic.comment.dedupl:
De-Duplicate any matching entities loaded into the Schematic World.

The current code tries to spawn the entities with their exact
UUID and EntityID if they were saved; so we needed a new
mechanism to manage duplicate UUID's and Entity ID's.
This config when disabled, adds any secondary copies of
the same Entity with a new random UUID.

Enabling this will be useful if you want to ensure that
your Schematic Entities fully match their original values;
such as when pasting the same minecart multiple times over,
and doing so might break your redstone.

This causes the Easy Place mode to place the first/closest block
you are looking at first, instead of the furthest/bottom-most block.
Setting this to false allows you to place multiple layers "at once",

When enabled, then you can hold down the use key

without having to click on every block individually.

This changes real world blocks; it is not an automatic builder.
Some servers restrict Easy Place. Check the server rules first.

When enabled, the Easy Place mode uses the
"Post-Rewrite" code from 1.12.2 ornithe.
§6WARNING!  THIS IS EXPERIMENTAL

The type of "accurate placement protocol" to use.
- Auto: Uses v3 in single player, and by default Slabs-only in multiplayer,
  unless the server has Carpet mod that sends a 'carpet:hello'
  packet, in which case v2 is used on that server.
- Version 3: Only supported by Litematica itself (in single player) or with Servux.
- Version 2: Compatible with servers with the Carpet mod
  (either QuickCarpet by skyrising and DeadlyMC,
  or CarpetExtra in addition to FabricCarpet.
  And in both cases the 'accurateBlockPlacement' Carpet rule needs
  to be enabled on the server).
- Slabs only: Only fixes top slabs. Compatible with Paper servers.
- None: Does not modify coordinates.

If enabled, then Litematica handles the so called

litematica.config.generic.comment.pasteN:
Whether or not the NBT data of blocks is attempted to be restored,
and which method is used for that.
- Place & Data Modify will try to place the "NBT-picked" block
  near the player, and then use the data modify
  command to transfer the NBT data to the setblock'ed block
- Place & Clone will try to place the "NBT-picked" block
  near the player, and then clone it to the final location.
- Teleport & Place will try to teleport the player nearby and then
  directly place the NBT-picked item in the correct position.
Note that the teleport & place method doesn't currently work correctly/at all.
The recommended method is §ePlace & Data Modify§r, however for that to work
you will probably need to lower the pasteCommandLimit to 1 per tick and increase
the pasteCommandInterval to 1-4 ticks or something.
Thus you should only use this for pasting important blocks that need the data,
for example by making a schematic of just the inventories,
and then paste that with replace behavior set to None.

litematica.config.generic.comment.pasteU:
If enabled, then instead of only using individual /setblock commands,
the command-based Paste operation (which is used on servers)
will also try to use /fill commands for any continuous areas of the same block.
This has no effect in single player, since the mod sets the blocks directly
in the integrated server's world in and doesn't use commands at all.

This is a temporary hack workaround to use the command-based pasting
also in single player, which allows using the render layer limited
pasting in single player, which currently doesn't work with
the direct world access pasting that single player normally uses.

Note that this will have all the same NBT data restoration
limitations that multiplayer pasting has normally.

Use Servux to paste a schematic directly to the server.
This method is much faster than the traditional
command-based method, and it supports restoring
Entity NBT Data.
§6NOTE: This feature requires '§dentityDataSync§6' to be enabled via Servux on servers.§r

litematica.config.generic.comment.placem:
Adjust the Placement Manager Thread performance metrics as follows:

MAX - 32 tasks per cycle (20ms yield, 2048 deferred cap)
DEFAULT - 16 tasks per cycle (50ms yield, 1024 deferred cap)
MINIMAL - 8 tasks per cycle (100ms yield, 512 deferred cap)
POTATO - 4 task per cycle (150ms yield, 128 deferred cap)

Lower profiles reduce CPU load and prevent frame drops on weaker
systems, but chunk rebuilds will take noticeably longer to complete.

Set the max number of Placement Manager Threads
NOTE: The default value (§e0§r) safely scales to your
system's CPU core count, and the actual thread usage
can be seen by enabling the §bdebugHudPMThreads§r
config for your F3 screen.
§6NOTE: Just because you can technically allocate
§616 threads, doesn't mean you should.
§eGenerally, 2 or 4 should be enough for most users.

The block replace behavior when adding blocks
to the schematic world.

This allows using overlapped placements without the
later handled placement always overwriting earlier ones with air.
On the other hand some blocks like light blocks are considered
to be air, so they would need the "All" replace behavior
to get placed at all.

litematica.config.generic.comment.unhide:
Un-hides the Schematic VCS (Version Control System) menu button,
and enables the hotkey and the VCS functionality in general.
(This was called Schematic Projects before.)

In general you §6should not§r be using this feature,
unless you really know how it works and what it does.
It somewhat changes how the area selections, placements and pasting works,
in particular that there is also an area delete operation when pasting.

Basically this feature is intended for §6iterative, in-place§r design work,
and it allows you to easier create multiple versions/snapshots
of the same build, and also to switch between the versions by deleting what is
in the world first, and then pasting the next version in its place.

litematica.gui.ux.keys.tip: View, search, and change your keyboard shortcuts.
litematica.gui.ux.home.mode.tip: Choose exactly what the tool does. Picking a mode does not run an operation. Existing scroll shortcuts still work.
litematica.gui.ux.home.tool.tip: Turn tool-item interactions on or off. Your choice is saved; this does not change the tool item or the separate requirement to hold it for world edits.
litematica.gui.ux.home.place.tip: Choose a schematic file, then position its ghost preview in your world. Previewing does not place real blocks.
litematica.gui.ux.home.save.tip: Select an area, edit its corners, then save it. One editor for this workflow.
litematica.gui.ux.home.build.tip: Manage placed previews and loaded schematics. Open a preview to adjust it, see materials, check your build or paste.
litematica.gui.ux.home.files.tip: Browse schematic files, edit their details, or convert formats. The original Schematic Manager is still here.
litematica.gui.ux.home.advanced.tip: Show running tasks and enabled versioned projects. Everyday tools live in the four main cards.
litematica.gui.ux.picker.title: Choose tool mode
litematica.gui.ux.picker.explain: Choose a mode; this runs no operation.
litematica.gui.ux.picker.area_selection: Select an area of your world to copy. Set the selection corners with your configured tool.
litematica.gui.ux.picker.schematic_place: Select and move a schematic's ghost preview. This does not place real blocks.
litematica.gui.ux.picker.fill: Creative only: fill the selected world area with the primary block when you execute the operation. Changes real blocks.
litematica.gui.ux.picker.replace_block: Creative only: replace matching blocks in the selected world area. Changes real blocks when executed.
litematica.gui.ux.picker.paste_schematic: Creative only: paste the selected schematic into the world when executed. This creates real blocks, not a ghost preview.
litematica.gui.ux.picker.grid_paste: Creative only: paste repeated grid placements into the world when executed. This changes real blocks.
litematica.gui.ux.picker.move: Creative only: move a selected area of real world blocks when executed. The original area may be cleared.
litematica.gui.ux.picker.delete: Creative only: delete real blocks in the selected area or placement when executed. Check the target first.
litematica.gui.ux.picker.rebuild: Edit blocks in the loaded schematic, not your real-world build. Also called Rebuild mode; save a copy before large edits.
litematica.gui.ux.build.materials.tip: Open the material list for the selected preview. If none is selected, reopen the last viewed list.
litematica.gui.ux.build.verify.tip: Compare the selected schematic placement with your world to find missing, wrong, or extra blocks. Select a placement first.
litematica.gui.ux.build.layers.tip: Show the whole ghost preview, one layer, or a range of layers. This does not change world blocks.
litematica.gui.ux.build.easy.tip: Toggle Easy Place. It helps pick the needed block while you build; it is not an automatic paste. You still need materials in Survival. Respect server rules and check Easy Place settings and shortcuts.
litematica.gui.ux.build.placements.tip: Open Schematic Placements and select the preview you want to build or check.
litematica.gui.ux.save.mode.tip: Switch Simple/Normal selection mode. Simple uses one box; Normal supports named selections with multiple boxes. Existing project behavior is unchanged.
litematica.gui.ux.save.edit.tip: Open the Area Editor to set corners and name your selection. In Normal mode, choose or create a selection in the browser first.
litematica.gui.ux.save.browse.tip: Create, select, and manage named area selections. Not available while a schematic project is open.
litematica.gui.ux.save.write.tip: Open the existing save dialog. Requires a world and a selection with at least one box. Nothing is written until you choose a file name and save.
litematica.gui.ux.help.title: Welcome to Litematica
litematica.gui.ux.help.page0.title: 1. Start from the home menu
litematica.gui.ux.help.page0.line1: Place, copy, manage ghosts, or browse files.
litematica.gui.ux.help.page0.line2: Open a ghost for all its placement tools.
litematica.gui.ux.help.page1.title: 2. Place a ghost preview
litematica.gui.ux.help.page1.line1: Choose Place a schematic, then a file.
litematica.gui.ux.help.page1.line2: A ghost preview does not place real blocks.
litematica.gui.ux.help.page2.title: 3. Hold your configured tool
litematica.gui.ux.help.page2.line1: Choose a tool mode on the home screen.
litematica.gui.ux.help.page2.line2: Hold the tool to select or move in-world.
litematica.gui.ux.help.dismiss: Open home; don't show welcome again
litematica.gui.ux.help.dismiss.tip: Save your choice. The introduction is always available from Help. Escape returns without permanently dismissing it.
litematica.gui.ux.advanced.loaded_schema: Manage schematics already loaded into memory. Create placements or unload them here.
litematica.gui.ux.advanced.schematic_pla: Manage ghost previews in this world: select, configure, enable, or remove placements.
litematica.gui.ux.advanced.load_schemati: Open the original file browser. Load a schematic into memory without the guided placement flow.
litematica.gui.ux.advanced.area_editor: Edit the current area selection and its corners. In Normal mode, create or select an area first.
litematica.gui.ux.advanced.area_selectio: Manage named area selections. Not available while a schematic project is open.
litematica.gui.ux.advanced.task_manager: Inspect and stop running Litematica background tasks.
litematica.gui.ux.advanced.schematic_pro: Open the legacy schematic project manager. This experimental workflow changes area-selection behavior.
litematica.gui.quick_place.next_tip: Read this schematic, then choose where to place its ghost. Nothing is placed yet.
litematica.gui.quick_place.legacy_tip: Open the original browser: load, rename, convert and open material lists. Its own Create placement checkbox still applies.
litematica.gui.quick_place.cancel_tip: Leave without loading or placing the selected file.
litematica.gui.quick_place.files_hint: No files? Add .litematic files to schematics/.
litematica.gui.quick_place.world_changed: The world changed or no world is open. Close this guide and start again in your world.
litematica.gui.quick_place.ghost_only: Ghost preview only — no world blocks change.
litematica.gui.quick_place.here_tip: Create one ghost preview at the block you are standing in. This does not paste blocks.
litematica.gui.quick_place.coordinates_t: Enter absolute whole-number X, Y and Z block coordinates. Nothing is placed until you confirm.
litematica.gui.quick_place.confirm_coord: Create the ghost at these coordinates. The anchor must be inside the world height and border.
litematica.gui.quick_place.load_only_tip: Keep this exact schematic in Loaded Schematics without creating any ghost placement.
litematica.gui.quick_place.back_tip: Go back without placing anything. The chosen schematic is kept for this guide, not loaded again.
litematica.gui.quick_place.invalid_coord: Enter whole numbers: X/Z between -29999999 and 29999999, Y between %s and %s. Relative (~) coordinates are not supported.
litematica.gui.quick_place.outside_world: The ghost anchor must be inside this world’s build height and world border.
litematica.gui.quick_place.removed: This schematic or placement was removed. Close the guide and start again.
litematica.gui.quick_place.rotate_tip: Turn the whole ghost clockwise around its anchor. Locked placements cannot be changed.
litematica.gui.quick_place.mirror_tip: Cycle the ghost through no mirror, left/right and front/back. Locked placements cannot be changed.
litematica.gui.quick_place.axis_locked: That coordinate is locked. Open More options to change the coordinate lock.
litematica.gui.quick_place.materials_tip: Count materials and missing blocks for this exact ghost placement.
litematica.gui.quick_place.more_tip: Open full placement settings: locks, anchor coordinates, sections, rendering, entities and verifier.
litematica.gui.quick_place.layers_tip: Open all render-layer controls. Layers affect every ghost, not the real world.
litematica.gui.quick_place.all_layers_ti: Show every layer of all ghost previews. No world blocks change.
litematica.gui.quick_place.layer_slider_: Dragging switches all ghosts to one horizontal Y layer and turns off follow-player. Use Show all layers to restore full ghosts.
litematica.gui.quick_place.done_tip: Keep this ghost and its adjustments. Return to the previous menu; Escape also keeps the ghost.
litematica.gui.quick_place.tool_help_tip: Enable the tool and select Place/Move Schematic mode for this ghost. Read the instructions, then close the menu. Does not move any real blocks.
litematica.gui.quick_place.tool_instruct: Tool ready. Hold the configured %s (including its required components), close the menu, aim at a world block and press %s to move this ghost anchor. Locks still apply. This is click-to-move, not drag.
litematica.gui.quick_place.project_tool: Close the active schematic project before using the placement tool. Project mode redirects tool clicks to area selection.
litematica.gui.quick_place.render_tool: Global rendering is off. Use Restore preview visibility below, then Move with tool. Nudge buttons still work.
litematica.gui.quick_place.x_minus_tip: Move this ghost one block along negative X. Disabled when the placement or this coordinate is locked.
litematica.gui.quick_place.x_plus_tip: Move this ghost one block along positive X. Disabled when the placement or this coordinate is locked.
litematica.gui.quick_place.y_minus_tip: Move this ghost one block along negative Y. Disabled when the placement or this coordinate is locked.
litematica.gui.quick_place.y_plus_tip: Move this ghost one block along positive Y. Disabled when the placement or this coordinate is locked.
litematica.gui.quick_place.z_minus_tip: Move this ghost one block along negative Z. Disabled when the placement or this coordinate is locked.
litematica.gui.quick_place.z_plus_tip: Move this ghost one block along positive Z. Disabled when the placement or this coordinate is locked.
litematica.gui.ux.home.place.short: Choose a file and position its preview
litematica.gui.ux.home.save.short: Copy a build from your world
litematica.gui.ux.build.visibility.tip: Open rendering settings to restore hidden ghost blocks or change their appearance.
litematica.gui.ux.safety.project_paste:
Apply project '%s', version %s ('%s', %s regions)?
Delete entire volumes first, including entities: %s. Then paste this version with the current layer settings.
%s
This approves the whole sequence; no further paste prompt follows deletion. Blocks and contents may be lost. Failure or a changed context can leave a partial result. No automatic world undo.
litematica.gui.quick_place.coordinate_ti: %s: absolute whole-number block coordinate. Tab / Shift+Tab moves between fields and buttons; Enter or Space activates a focused button, never places while editing.
litematica.gui.quick_place.restore_previ: Preview hidden: one or more global rendering switches are off. Click to enable overall rendering, schematic rendering and schematic blocks for all previews. Layer filters, placement visibility and locks are unchanged; use Show all layers or More options if needed.
litematica.gui.quick_place.global_layers: Layers affect every ghost, not world blocks.
litematica.gui.ux.build.paste.tip: Paste the selected ghost placement as REAL blocks. Asks for confirmation first. Creative mode and a selected placement required.
litematica.gui.quick_place.paste_tip: Paste this ghost as REAL world blocks. Asks for confirmation first; this preview stays. Creative mode required.
litematica.gui.quick_place.browser_hint: Pick a schematic, then Next. Rename or open JSON/TXT lists in My schematics.
litematica.gui.quick_place.commit_failed: Could not finish loading or placing. Check Loaded schematics and placements before trying again.
litematica.gui.hover.ux.edit_layers: Choose which schematic layers are visible. This affects every preview, not world blocks.
litematica.gui.label.ux.search_all_setti: Search covers all settings and hotkeys
litematica.gui.baby.ghosts.previews.tip: Select a ghost preview, open its one editor, show/hide it or remove it.
litematica.gui.baby.ghosts.loaded.tip: Advanced: source objects in memory. Create another preview, save edits, reload or unload.
litematica.gui.baby.ghosts.help: Open a preview to adjust, build or paste it.
litematica.gui.baby.ghosts.loaded_help: Source schematics; unloading also removes their previews.
litematica.gui.placement_editor.title: Preview settings
litematica.gui.baby.ghosts.clear.tip: Clear the active area-selection boxes and origin. Simple mode stays ready for the next tool click; named saved areas are unselected, not deleted. Project selection geometry is reset. Ghost previews and world blocks are untouched.
litematica.gui.ux.home.layers.tip: Choose which schematic layers are visible. This affects every preview, not world blocks.
